title: Tiered SLI/SLO playbook and executable failover/circuit-breaker policy for model endpoints
creator: Carlos Nguyen
description: Create a prescriptive, tiered SLI/SLO framework and operational playbook that defines: per-endpoint and per-model SLIs, error budget burn policies, multi-region failover tiers, circuit-breaker thresholds, and automated load-shedding behavior. This ticket drives both the spec and the initial implementation hooks (metrics, dashboards, runbooks) required to roll the policy into production for the first set of critical model endpoints.
background: We currently have ad-hoc SLOs for some endpoints and multiple operational practices documented in separate repos. This causes inconsistent behavior during incidents (different teams use different thresholds and handoffs), unclear error budget ownership, and scattershot failover configurations. Customers have reported flapping availability during region outages and inconsistent circuit breaker responses during hot loops. We need a canonical, tiered policy tied to metric names, dashboards, and automated actions so the platform can behave predictably.
proposed_solution: Deliver a single playbook that maps endpoints/models to a tier (T1/T2/T3), defines SLIs with exact calculation formulas, sets SLO targets and error-budget burn thresholds, specifies automated circuit-breaker trip conditions and backoff, and prescribes multi-region failover tiers (hot/hot-warm/cold) and progressive load-shedding rules. Provide implementation artifacts: dashboard templates (Grafana), alert rules (Prometheus), runtime flags, and a small controller that applies circuit-breaker and shedding policies via our routing layer.
sli_definitions: Success rate (primary SLI): inference.success.rate = successful_responses / total_requests where successful_responses = responses with HTTP 2xx and model_response.error=false

Latency (latency SLI): inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 computed on request end-to-end (client request->complete tokens). Use 'inference.time_to_first_token' and 'inference.time_to_last_token' for streaming endpoints.
Quality (optional SLI for tuned models): inference.response-quality.regression_score computed via automated evals on a rolling prompt set for canary traffic.
System health (safety SLI): inference.kv_cache.hit_rate and inference.model.memory_pressure (proxied to node-level evictions) used as secondary indicators for error-budget churn.
slo_targets_and_tiers: Tier T1 (customer-facing low-latency API): availability SLO = 99.9% monthly; latency SLO p95 < 200ms; error budget burn triggers: 5% burn in 1 hour -> ops page; 15% burn in 1 hour -> automatic traffic reroute to warm region.

Tier T2 (internal tools / delayed UX): availability SLO = 99.5% monthly; latency SLO p95 < 500ms; error budget burn triggers: 10% burn in 1 hour -> alert + manual review; 25% burn in 6 hours -> enforce shed-noncritical traffic.
Tier T3 (best-effort batch / embeddings bulk jobs): availability SLO = 99.0% monthly; latency SLO p95 < 2000ms; error budget handled with relaxed shedding and long-window throttles.
Note: Per-model overrides allowed for premium enterprise customers (documented in release notes and attached as model annotation metadata).
error_budget_policy: Calculate monthly error budget as (1 - availability_slo) * total_requests for the SLO window.
Real-time burn rate = observed_errors / expected_errors over rolling windows (5m, 1h, 6h).
Escalation matrix: burn_rate > 2x for 30m -> warn on-call; burn_rate > 5x for 15m -> auto-fallback traffic; burn_rate sustained > 3x for 1h -> open incident and engage SRE.
Deployment gates: if current error_budget_remaining < 25%, block automated rollouts of model changes unless explicit staged approval is granted by SRE.
Recovery steps to reclaim budget: enable degraded mode (drop optional features), route to lower-cost model variant, or impose soft throttling for best-effort clients.
failover_and_region_policy: Define region roles per endpoint: primary (hot), secondary (warm), tertiary (cold). For T1 endpoints require at least one warm in-region or cross-region ready with model pinned to same version.

Failover sequence: 1) local model fallback (smaller quantized model), 2) route to warm region with sticky session preservation for streaming where possible, 3) if warm region capacity saturated -> cold failover with increased latency expectations and user-visible degradation notice.
Traffic steering: use adaptive routing policy with latency/capacity heuristics and model-compatibility tags. Heatmap dashboard will show region utilization and failover events for postmortem.
Practice drills: quarterly controlled failovers per critical endpoint with success criteria tracked in release playbooks.
circuit_breaker_and_load_shedding_policy: Circuit breaker states: CLOSED -> HALF_OPEN -> OPEN with clearly defined metrics for transition.
Trip conditions: open CB when (backend_error_rate > 5% AND request_qps > 1000) OR (p95_latency > configured_threshold for 3 consecutive intervals).

Backoff behavior: exponential backoff starting at 30s with jitter, and health-check probing on HALF_OPEN intervals. For streaming endpoints, close only after a sustained pass of time and monitored token progress.

Load-shedding rules: soft-shed at 70% CPU/GPU util per node by returning 429 with Retry-After for best-effort clients; hard-shed at 90% by rejecting long-running or low-priority requests and preserving T1 traffic. Use client priority headers for decisioning.
Graceful degradation: prefer prefix-KV cache hits and small-window responses; optionally reduce max tokens and model temperature for degraded mode.
telemetry_and_dashboard_changes: Add / standardize metrics: inference.request.total, inference.request.success, inference.request.error, inference.latency.p50/p95/p99, inference.kv_cache.hit_rate, inference.queue_length, node.gpu.utilization, model.version, model.variant.
Annotate metrics with 'tier' and 'endpoint_id' labels for per-tenant visibility.
Create dashboard templates: SLO Overview (per-endpoint), Error Budget Burn Rate, Region Failover Map, Circuit Breaker Events timeline.
Alert rules: critical when SLO violation probability > 95% within the next 1h based on forecasted burn (Prometheus alertmanager rule), and warning for early burn signals.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI formulas documented and reviewed by SRE and PM (sign-off in Confluence).
Dashboard templates deployed and populated with data for at least 3 critical endpoints (T1/T2 split).
Automated circuit-breaker controller prototype that honors configured trip/backoff rules and can be toggled via runtime flags in staging.
Failover choreography tested in staging with simulated region outage and recovery validated in runbook exercise.
Deployment gate hook implemented: pipeline blocks if monthly error budget remaining < 25% for the model/endpoint.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (spec & telemetry) - 2 weeks: finalize playbook, implement metrics and dashboard templates, add model/endpoint tier annotations.
Phase 2 (controller & gates) - 3 weeks: implement circuit-breaker controller, pipeline gate, and runtime flags in staging; run internal canaries.
Phase 3 (pilot) - 2 weeks: enable for 3 T1 endpoints and 2 T2 endpoints behind feature flag; run scheduled failover drills and iterate.
Phase 4 (platform-wide) - rollout over two release cycles with SRE-led postmortem after each controlled failover.
runbook_steps: 1) Detect: alert triggers for SLO burn and circuit-breaker OPEN state.
2) Triage: confirm region health, check model variant versions, inspect GPU memory pressure and KV cache hit rate.
3) Short-term mitigation: enable model fallback, route traffic to warm region, enable degraded response mode (truncate tokens, lower temperature).
4) Escalate: if automated mitigation insufficient, follow incident runbook and notify customer success for affected tenants.
5) Post-incident: annotate incident with error_budget consumption, update playbook if trip conditions produced false positives/negatives.
open_questions: How should we represent composite SLIs for hybrid endpoints (mix of streaming and synchronous)? Proposal: compute separate latency SLIs for TTF token and full-response and weight them by traffic pattern.
What is the canonical priority header set for client SDKs? Need agreement with SDK team (ENG-20301).
Do we allow customer-level overrides of automatic shedding? If yes, define opt-out constraints and audit controls.
